title: Functional Error Representation
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of functional error representation using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Functional Error Representation** as part of **Functional Programming and Idiomatic Kotlin**. Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions. Use the subtopics—Results as Values, Nullable Results Versus Explicit Outcomes, Sealed Result Models—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with results as values. Then compare it with nullable results versus explicit outcomes. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Nullable Results Versus Explicit Outcomes
items.text: Nullable Results Versus Explicit Outcomes is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.
